key_facts: The document applies to all teams and officials at the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix, held 30 October – 1 November 2026.

Drivers must not exceed a maximum time set by the Stewards between the Second Safety Car Line and the First Safety Car Line during qualifying, in-laps, out-laps, and reconnaissance laps, or they may be deemed to be going unnecessarily slowly.
Drivers caught by a faster car must allow it to pass at the first available opportunity; blue light panels will warn them when the faster car is within 1.2 seconds.
Several track limits apply: at Turn 17, Turn 4, and Turn 11; breaches may result in lap time invalidation.
Safety Car deployment will be signalled by the message 'SAFETY CAR DEPLOYED' and trackside light panels displaying 'SC', not by waved yellow flags or 'SC' boards.
plain_explanation:
This document sets out the rules for running the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix. It covers how drivers should behave during qualifying and the race, what happens in specific areas of the track and pit lane, and how the race will be managed.

Drivers must not drive unnecessarily slowly during qualifying or reconnaissance laps. The Stewards will set a maximum time between the Second Safety Car Line and the First Safety Car Line; any driver who exceeds this time on any lap during or after qualifying, or during reconnaissance laps when the pit exit opens for the race, may be penalised. This rule applies to in-laps and out-laps as well, and includes the pit lane.

When a faster driver is catching up to a slower driver during the race, the slower driver must allow the faster driver to overtake at the first available opportunity. A marshalling system will give a pre-warning when the faster car is within 3.0 seconds. When the faster car is within 1.2 seconds, blue light panels will be shown to the slower car, along with blue cockpit lights and a message on the timing monitors.

The document gives detailed instructions about the pit lane, the grid, and how practice starts may be carried out. There are specific rules about where cars must stop during a race suspension and where they can re-enter the track after going off.

There are track limits at three locations. At Turn 17, a breach may result in that lap time and the immediately following lap time being invalidated. At Turn 4, if a driver misses the apex and crosses a solid yellow line with all four wheels, they must re-join the circuit after Turn 5 using the asphalt rejoin route, not the grass. At Turn 11, if a driver's car passes completely behind the red and white kerb at the apex, they must re-join by keeping to the right of the first polystyrene block arrangement and then to the left of the second.

When the Safety Car is deployed, all competitors will receive the message "SAFETY CAR DEPLOYED" and all trackside light panels will display "SC". Waved yellow flags and "SC" boards will not be used. When the Safety Car is withdrawn, the message "SAFETY CAR LIGHTS OFF" will be sent and a green light panel will be displayed at the Control Line.

The document also lists changes made to the circuit for this event, including resurfacing, new blue lines at several points, and changes to the practice start boxes.
